relevance.rationale: The corpus block rem:q-dilog-three-contexts asserts, with NO citation, that the q-dilogarithm has three simultaneous realisations: a truncated F_p form Li_2^{q,(p)}(x) = sum_{n=1}^{p-1} x^n/(n [n]_q), and convergent Q_p / C_p forms on v_p(x) > 1/(p-1). The q=1 shadow of exactly that finite-vs-p-adic pairing is what Besser proves: the finite polylogarithm li_n (the (p-1)-truncation) is the mod-p reduction of a Coleman p-adic Li_n. This supplies the missing literature backing for the F_p <-> C_p bridge the block asserts, and Cor. 2.2 gives the p-adic valuation of Li_n at roots of unity, which is the p-adic counterpart of the cyclotomic Li_3(zeta_5^k) values the appendix-surreals blocks manipulate. It is background/technique, not a result any QOU derivation consumes: Besser is at q=1, so it does not by itself establish the q-deformed statement the block makes.

keyResults.statement: For Li_n^{(p)}(z) := Li_n(z) - Li_n(z^p)/p^n one has Li_n^{(p)}(X) subset W, and Li_n^{(p)} reduces mod p to (1 - z^p)^{-1} li_n(z), where li_n(z) = sum_{k=1}^{p-1} z^k/k^n is the finite polylogarithm.
keyResults.useForFolio: Gives the q=1 literature backing for rem:q-dilog-three-contexts' unsourced claim that the (p-1)-truncated F_p dilogarithm and the C_p-convergent dilogarithm are two faces of one object; makes explicit that the correct bridge carries a (1 - z^p)^{-1} factor and a Frobenius-twisted argument, neither of which the block currently records.

keyResults.statement: For a root of unity alpha in X, Li_n(alpha) lies in p^n W and p^{-n} Li_n(alpha) is congruent mod p to -li_n(sigma(alpha))/(1 - alpha).
keyResults.useForFolio: The p-adic valuation of polylogarithms at roots of unity — the direct p-adic analogue of the cyclotomic values Li_3(zeta_5^k) that conj:bring-trilog-depth-3-witness and prop:cl3-zeta5-orbit-sum-identity manipulate archimedeanly. Usable as a remark noting that the orbit-sum relations have a p-adic shadow with a computable valuation, not as an input to any current derivation.
